items.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: we did three twelve inch LPs of Irving Berlin things on the occasion of his eightieth birthday

ctx.x: That’s interesting. Do you have any idea of how many recordings you played on?

Not really. I have a lot that I played on and I have at least maybe a dozen albums that I had done the arranging and so-called leading on, which are under my own name. Some of them are more of a feature thing like this — or I did a lot of recordings of, this record company was interested in doing mostly songwriters. I never really knew much about songwriters or cared much until working for this record company, Monmouth Evergreen Records, we did three twelve inch LPs of Irving Berlin things on the occasion of his…
Well I have a list out of one of the jazz recording books and it has your eight or nine recordings between 1955 and ‘65. Those were good years for you.
